appraisal_events.evidence: Robert tells the narrator: "C'est à mourir de rire. Jusqu'au chien du logis, il s'efforce de complaire. C'est d'autant plus drôle que mon oncle déteste les gigolos. Et regarde comme il les écoute avec sérieux. Si c'était moi qui avais voulu les lui présenter, ce qu'il m'aurait envoyé dinguer."
appraisal_events.explanation: Robert exposes the gap between Charlus's affected reluctance and stated contempt for young dandies and his eager, deferential courting of Mme de Surgis's sons, comically deflating Charlus's pose of haughty indifference; this reading matches the narrator's own earlier characterization of Charlus's contradictory affect toward young men.

status_effects.explanation: Charlus's carefully performed hauteur and feigned indifference are exposed by Robert as hypocritical eagerness, locally deflating his stance even as he continues to control the surface interaction with Mme de Surgis.

ambiguities: Robert's exposure of Charlus's hypocrisy is delivered as his own amused private aside to the narrator; how far the narrator's own voice endorses (rather than merely relays) this reading is not fully certain, though it is consistent with the narrator's earlier analysis of Charlus's contradictory affect toward young men.
